newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul bans Taiwan pork, beef imports on disease.
newsitem.headline: Seoul bans Taiwan pork, beef imports on disease.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of Agricuture and Forestry said on Friday it had banned imports of cloven-hoofed animals and related products from Taiwan indefinitely due to an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease there.

"We received a notice on the break from the Taiwanese authorities at 6:00 p.m. (0900 GMT) on Thursday and decided to ban the imports from Thursday," an official at the Agriculture and Forestry Ministry told Reuters.

The ministry also ordered the state-run National Animal Quarantine Service and the National Veterinarian Research Institute to closely monitor previously contracted imports of cloven-hoofed animals and products including pork, the ministry official said.

The official said the outbreak was expected to help South Korea's pork exports to Japan since Taiwan supplies 40.8 percent of Japan's total pork imports. South Korea's pork exports to Japan totalled 36,700 tonnes in 1996.

Taiwan on Thursday banned all pork exports following the outbreak of the highly contagious foot-and-mouth disease in its hog population, spelling huge losses for one of the island's export industries.
Since the beginning of this year, South Korea has imported 2,068 tonnes of pork including 36 tonnes under the Minimum Market Access requirement of the World Trade Organisation.
South Korea's imports of pork totalled 1,497 tonnes in 1996.
